  TRANSPORTATION  AUTHORITY  TO  REPROGRAM  FUNDS  FOR  ADDITIONAL
  IMPROVEMENTS  ON IMPERIAL  HIGHWAY

  PURPOSE:  To authorize  Amendment  No.  2 to Contract  No.  2020-02-CC  ("Amendment  No.
  2")  the  Measure  R  Funding  Agreement  with  the  Los  Angeles  County  Metropolitan
  Transportation  Authority  ("LACMTA"),  allowing  the City  of South  Gate ("City")  to reprogram
  the remaining  balance  of $89,594  in Measure  R funds  to the next phase of construction  of street
  improvements  on Imperial  Highway.

  RECOMMENDATION  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No.  2  to  Contract  No.  2020-02-CC,  Measure  R  Funding
  Agreement  with  the  Los  Angeles  County  Metropolitan  Transportation  Authority
  ("LACMTA"),  to reprogram  $89,594  in remaining  funds  from  the Imperial  Highway
  Improvements  (Phase  %), City  Project  No.  496-ST,  Metro  Project  ID No.  MR306.57,  to
  the Imperial  Highway  Improvements  (Phase  II),  City  Project  No.  699-ST,  Metro  Project
  ID No. MR306.57,  for additional  median  improvements;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No.  2 to Contract  No.  2020-02-CC  in a
  form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the City's  General  Fund.  A total  of  $89,594  in
  Measure  R funds  will  be reprogrammed  to the second phase of construction  of improvements  on
  Imperial  Highway  (City  Project  No. 699-ST,  LACMTA  Project  ID MR306.57).

  ANALYSIS:  Construction  of Phase  I of the Imperial  Highway  improvements  was completed
  under  budget,  leaving  a balance  of $89,594  in Measure  R funds.  Approval  of Amendment  No. 2
  to  the  Measure  R Funding  Agreement  (Contract  No.  2020-02-CC)  will  allow  the  City  to
  reprogram  these  remaining  funds  toward  a second  phase  of  improvements  along  Imperial
  Highway.  This next phase includes  modifying  the existing  median  to add a new left-turn  pocket,
  which  will  enhance  access to properties  on the south  side of the corridor.  These  improvements
  aim  to support  traffic  safety,  circulation,  and access.  Amendment  No.  2 updates  the funding
  agreement  to reflect  the following:

  1  215
   Reprogramming  of  the  remaining  $89,594  in  Measure  R  funds  for  the  median
  modification;

  *  Extension  of the funding  lapse date to June 30, 2029;  and

  *  A revised  scope  of work  that  includes:  (a) Construction  of  a new  westbound  U-turn
  pocket  approximately  670 feet east of the Los Angeles  River;  (b) Median  and pavement
  enhancements;  (c)  Traffic  signal  timing  modifications  at the  intersection  of  Imperial
  Highway  and Garfield  Avenue;  and (d) Construction  support  and management  services.

BACKGROUND:  On January  14, 2021,  the City  Council  approved  the Measure  R Funding
Agreement  with  LACMTA  (Contract  No.  2020-02-CC),  accepting  $1,456,250  in Measure  R
funds  for  the  Imperial  Highway  Corridor  Improvements  Project.  The  project  was  completed
under  budget,  resulting  in a surplus  of $490,000.

On March  29, 2022,  the City  Council  approved  Amendment  No.  1 to the Measure  R Funding
Agreement,  which  de-obligated  the  $490,000  in  surplus  funds  and reallocated  them  toward
improvements  along  Garfield  Avenue  and additional  enhancements  along  Imperial  Highway.
Following  the completion  of those improvements,  a remaining  balance  of $89,594  in Measure  R
funds remained  unspent.

On  January  23,  2025,  the  LACMTA  Board  approved  Amendment  No.  2 to the Measure  R
Funding  Agreement,  authorizing  the reprogramming  of the remaining  funds  for the construction
of a new westbound  U-turn  pocket  on Imperial  Highway,  approximately  670 feet east of the Los
Angeles  River.  To  implement  this  change,  City  Council  approval  of  Amendment  No.  2 is
required.

Construction  is scheduled  to begin  in October  2025 and be completed  by December  2025.

 BACKGROUND:  The City is served by storm drain systems owned and operated by both the
Los Angeles County Flood Control District ("LACFCD")  and the City. Together, these systems
include 836 catch basins, of which 39 are City-owned and the remaining  are owned by the
County.

The Department of Public Works is responsible for maintaining the City's municipal storm drain
system and utilizes a contractor to perfon'n catch basin maintenance. Additionally,  under
Contract No. 2817 approved by the City Council in 2012, the City is obligated to maintain  catch
basins owned by the LACFCD.  City staff will invoice LACFCD  for the cost of regular
maintenance  services  provided.

Maintenance activities must comply with the requirements of the Federal Clean Water Act
("CWA")  and the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System ("NPDES") Permit. To meet
these standards, industrial vacuum tnicks are used to clean storm drains and catch basins. These
vehicles utilize high-powered suction systems to extract debris, sludge, and standing water. The
material is then contained in the truck's holding tank for transport and proper disposal.

Currently, the City contracts with RMI for these services under the Agreement, which was
approved on July 26, 2022, for a three-year term in the amount of $400,860. The contract is set
to expire on July 25, 2025.

Under this Agreement, RMI is responsible for inspecting, maintaining and stenciling 836 catch
basins. Catch basins are cleaned six times annually, once during the dry season and five times
during the wet season. Each cleaning cycle is completed over a one-month period, ensuring
consistent monthly maintenance during the wet season.

Additionally,  RMI maintains the City's 14 Filterra units. These specialized drainage devices,
located throughout the public right-of-way, are designed to capture stormwater runoff and treat it
through a filtration process, reducing pollutants before the water is either absorbed into the
ground or discharged into the storm drain system.

 ANALYSIS:  The City  of South  Gate ("City")  contracts  with  Mariposa  to maintain  landscaped
street medians  along  major  roadways,  as well  as other  City-owned  properties,  including  parking
lots and tree wells.  This amendment  will  expand  Mariposa's  scope of work  to include  maintenance
of newly  constructed  street medians  and a one-time  median  restoration  project.

Now  that the establishment  period  for the newly  constructed  landscape  medians  on Long  Beach
Boulevard  and  Garfield  Boulevard  have  expired,  the  City  is responsible  for  their  ongoing
maintenance.  Amendment  No.  I provides  $133,908,  aru'iually  for maintenance  of the new center
medians  on these two  corridors  and $42,000, annually  for maintenance  on the median  located  at
the intersection  of Garfield  and Miller  Way.  The total  annual  maintenance  costs for these median
sites are $175,908.

AdditionalJy,  over  the past several  years,  the condition  of the landscaped  medians,  particularly
along  Firestone  Boulevard  and at the intersection  of Garfield  Avenue  and Miller  Way,  have
noticeably  deteriorated,  impacting  their appearance  and reducing  the overall  visual  quality  of these
prominent  corridors.  Amendment  No.  I includes  a one-time  median  restoration  project,  totaling
(a) $83,639  for road medians  along  Firestone  Boulevard;  (b) $4,900  for a road median  located  at
the intersection  of Garfield  Avenue  and Miller  Way;  (c) $10,000  contingency  fee for unexpected
costs or unforeseen  issues related  to the restoration  project,  and (d) a one-time  cost of $1,015  for
the purchase  and installation  of an irrigation  control  unit  for preserving  median  vegetation.  The
total restoration  costs are $99,554.

For Fiscal  Year 2025/26,  the total annuar maintenance  and restoration  cost is $275,462.  For Fiscal
Year  2026/27,  the  total  annual  maintenance  cost  is $175,908.  The  total  combined  cost  for
Amendment  1 is $451,370.  This  brings  the overall  contract  value  to $1,812,386,  which  includes
the original  contract  amount  of $1,361,016  and $451,370  from  Amendment  1.

BACKGROUND:  The City is responsible  for maintaining  a variety  of public  spaces and facilities
located  along  streets  and  sidewalks.  These  include  landscaped  center  medians,  vacant  lots,
retaining  walls,  bus stops, sidewalks,  parking  lots, and commercial  corridors  such as Tweedy  Mile
and the Hollydale  Shopping  Center.  Regular  landscaping  and general  maintenance  are essential  to
ensuring  these areas remain  clean,  safe, and visually  appealing.

On October  22, 2024, the City  Council  approved  a three-year  agreement  with  Mariposa  Landscape
Services,  LLC,  in the amount  of $1,361,016  for landscaping  and maintenance  of various  City-
owned  properties,  including  landscape  medians.

At  the  time  the  Agreement  was  approved,  newly  constructed  medians  along  Long  Beach
Boulevard,  Garfield  Avenue,  and other  locations  were  not yet included  in the contract,  as they
were  still  under  the maintenance  responsibility  of the construction  contractor  during  the 120-  to
180-day  plant  establishment  period.  With  the expiration  of those  periods,  the City  must  now
assume  maintenance  responsibility.  Amendment  No. 1 to the Agreement  provides  the necessary
services  to support  both ongoing  and one-time  landscape  improvements.

  SUBJECT:  AMENDMENT  N0.  1  TO  CONTRACT  N0.  2025-26-AC  FOR
  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  WITH  WILLDAN  ENGINEERING  FOR  STAFF
  AUGMENT  ATION

  PURPOSE:  To approve  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2025-26-AC  ("Amendment  No. 1")
  with  Willdan  Engineering  ("Willdan")  to continue  staff  augmentation  services  until  the vacant
  Street and Sewer  Superintendent  position  is filled,  for up to nine (9) months.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No.  1 to Contract  No.  2025-26-AC  with  Willdan  Engineering
  ("Agreement")  to extend  the term of the contract  on a month-to-month  basis for up to nine
  (9) months,  to continue  staff  augmentation  services  until  the vacant  Street  and Sewer
  Superintendent  position  is filled,  for a not to exceed  amount  of $126,277;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No.  1 in a form  acceptable  to the City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Amendment  No.  I to the Agreement  will  be funded  with  $126,277  General
  Fund salary savings  from  the budgeted  vacant  Street and Sewer  Superintendent  position.  The total
  revised  contract  amount  is $176,257.

  ANALYSIS:  On  June  13,  2023,  the  City  Council  approved  a policy  authorizing  staff  to
  temporarily  fund  contract  staff augmentation  services  using  salary  savings  from  vacant  positions
  ("Policy").  Under  this authority,  the City  Manager  administratively  approved  Contract  No. 2025-
  26-AC  to provide  staff  augmentation  services  to temporarily  fill  the vacant  Street  and Sewer
  Superintendent  position.  The contract  provides  for an interim  Superintendent  on a part-time  basis,
  scheduled  at 24 hours per week for a term  of three (3) months.

  The Field  Operations  Division  is actively  working  to fill  the Superintendent  vacancy;  however,
  the recruitment  process  is expected  to extend  beyond  the expiration  of Contract  No. 2025-26-AC.
  Amendment  No. 1 will  allow  services  to continue  on a month-to-month  basis until  the position  is
  filled.  In accordance  with  City policy,  this continued  service  is proposed  to be fiinded  with  General
  Fund salary savings  from  the vacant  position,  estimated  at $126,277 over the next nine (9) months.

  BACKGROUND:  The Street and Sewer  Superintendent  is a key leadership  position  witin  the
  Public  Works  Department,  responsible  for overseeing  the daily  operations  of the Field  Operations

  1

  256
 Division,  including  the maintenance  and repair  of streets,  sidewalks,  storm  drains,  sewers,  trees
and right-of-way  infrastructure.  The  Superintendent  ensures  that work  is scheduled  efficiently,
crews  are properly  staffed  and equipped,  and that projects  and maintenance  activities  are executed
in alignment  with  City  standards,  safety  protocols,  and service  expectations.  This position  serves
as a critical  bridge  between  high-level  management  and  field-level  operations,  translating
departmental  goals  into  actionable  work  plans  and supervising  frontline  supervisors  and field
crews.

When  the position  became  vacant  in January  of 2025,  the Deputy  Director  of Public  Works,
temporarily  absorbed  the  Superintendent's  duties.  While  this  stopgap  maintained  operational
continuity,  it also had negative  impacts.  The Deputy  Director  has had to divert  attention  from
higher-level  planning,  performance  management,  and strategic  oversight  of the entire  yard  to
address  day-to-day  operational  matters  typically  managed  by the Superintendent.  This  shift  in
focus  has disrupted  the  Deputy  Director's  ability  to effectively  manage  long-term  priorities,
oversee  capital  project  coordination,  and lead departmental  initiatives.

As such, on May  12, 2025,  the City  Manager  administratively  approved  Contract  No.  2025-26-
AC  with  Willdan  in the amount  of $49,980  temporarily  fill  the position  with  staff  augmentation
services.  The Agreement  has a term of three (3) months;  however,  the recruitment  process  will  be
completed  after this term end. As such, Amendment  No. 1 to the Agreement  provides  an additional
$126,277  for services  on a month-to-month  basis.

Continuing  the use of contract  staff  augmentation  is vital  to keep  operational  balance,  ensure
consistent  field  oversight,  and  allow  department  leadership  to  function  at the  appropriate
managerial  level.

  SUBJECT:  HVAC  EQUIPMENT  RENT  AL  SERVICES  WITH  HERC  RENT  ALS,  INC.,
  TO PROVIDE  TEMPORARY  COOLING  AT  THE  POLICE  STATION

  PURPOSE:  To authorize  the City Manager  to approve  a Purchase  Order  with HBRC  Rentals,  Inc.
  for temporary  HVAC  equipment  rentals.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  co'nsider  Authorizing  the City  Manager
  to approve  a Purchase  Order  with HERC  Rentals,  Inc. to fund equipment  rentals  needed to operate  -:
  the HVAC  systems  at the Police  Station  Detective  Bureau  and Main  Jail  Areas  for  $I4,286
  monthly,  for up to a seven-month  period  and an amount  not to exceed  $100,002.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  The Purchase  Order is in the amount  of $100,002,  and it will  be 'junded  with
  General  Funds  budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year 2024/25  Capital  Improvement  Program.

  ANALYSIS:  The HVAC  systems  at City Hall  and the Police  Station  were installed  over 30 years
  ago, resulting  in ongoing  reliability  issues  that  led to system  failures  during  the hot  summer
  months.  To address these concerns,  significant  repairs  and upgrades  were completed  over the past
  fiscal  year. This work  included,  but was not limited  to, the installation  of a new chiller  system  and
  a 5-ton unit at the Police  Station,  as well  as a new air handler  and cooling  tower  at City Hall.

  Additional  improvements  to the HVAC  system  at the Police  Station  are currently  in the design
  phase and are scheduled  for completion  in the next  fiscal  year.  Specifically,  enhancements  and
  expansion  of the HVAC  system  serving  the main jail  area are planned,  as the current  system  has
  reliability  issues  that  leave  portions  of the  facility  without  adequate  cooling.  The  proposed
  Purchase  Order  with  HERC  will  provide  temporary  HVAC  equipment  rentals  to ensure  proper
  climate  control  in the main jail  area until  during  the summer  months  anticipated  in 2025.

  BACKGROUND:  The Police  Station  Detective  Bureau  and Main  Jail Areas  are equipped  with
  HVAC  systems  that are more than 30-years  old. These systems  fail regularly  and are near the end
  of their  service  life and they shut down  regularly  within  the hot summer  months  when demand  is
  high.  They  provide  inadequate  or no cooling  to maintain  comfortable  temperatures  in these areas
  when the outside  air temperature  exceeds  85 degrees  Fahrenheit.

  I

  262
 The standard industry norm for HVAC equipment lifespan is 20 years and in the milder conditions
of California, 25 years is the accepted norm based on many decades of experience.  These systems
are past the California standard of 25 years. These systems experience  performance reliability
issues and tend to fail in the suinmer seasons, thereby placing at risk essential public services.

Honeywell as part of phase 2 repairs and enhancements for the South Gate Police Department is
investigating system repair options for the Detective Bureau's Air Handler Unit to improve
performance and reliability. Completion of these repairs is estimated to be October of 2025 at an
estimated cost of approximately $400,000.

The Public Works Engineering Division has retained a design consultant for the South Gate Police
Department Detection Center. Design will be completed in approximately  sixty days with
construction starting around October of 2025 with an estimated completion of May of 2026 and
an cost estimate of approximately $1.1 Million.

The Department of Public Works obtained services from HERC Rental, Inc. through Omnia
Partners Cooperative Contract Purchasing Program (Contract No. 2019000318), pursuant  to
Purchasing Ordinance guidelines: 1.54.510 Exemptions from formal and informal bidding
procedures, with administrative approval of the City Manager to acquire the needed equipment. In
this case, the exempt falls under Section 1.54.510.D (Cooperative Purchasing). The estimated
rental period is for up to seven months depending on weather conditions. Total rental charges and
fees are determined by quotes received.

CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  JULY  8, 2025

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria  Davila,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order at
  6:46 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley,  Director  Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice  Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City Attorney  Raul F. Salinas,
  Assistant  City  Manager  Arturo  Cervantes

EXCUSED/ABSENT  City  Manager  Rob Houston

l
COMMUNITY  DEV/

HOUSING  Following  the conclusion  of the Public  Hearing,  the City  Council:

  a.  Adopted  Resolution  No. 2025-22-CC  Resolution  of the City  Council
  of the City  of South  Gate, California,  receiving  and approving  the
  Five-Year  2025-2029  Consolidated  Plan and Fiscal  Year 2025-2026
  Annual  Action  Plan;

  b.  Authorizing  the City  Manager,  or designee,  to submit  to the U.S.
  Department  of Housing  and Urban  Development  the Five-Year  2025-
  2029 Consolidated  Plan and FY 2025-2026  Annual  Action  Plan (as
  amended);  and

  c.  Authorizing  the City  Manager,  or designee,  to enter into agreements
  with  eligible  subrecipients  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

  Carol Averell,  Housing  Manager,  gave the presentation.

  Mayor  Davila  asked if anyone  in the audience  wished  to speak on this
  item.  Seeing  no one step forward;  Mayor  Davila  closed  the audience
  portion.

EMAILS  Mario  Dominguez  urges the City  Council  to allocate  CDBG  funding  to the
  Department  of Parks and Recreation.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JTJLY  8, 2025

l
COMM[iNITY  DEV /

HOUSING  CONT'D  Edgar  Pelayo  advocates  for the CDBG  funding  to be used for the Parks
  and Recreation  Department.

RECESS  Prior  to the conclusion  of item 1, the City  Council  recessed  at 7:00 p.m.,
  and reconvened  at 8:57 p.m., with  all Members  of Council  present.

  Council  MemberAvalos  questioned  how this business  has been conducted
  for the last five years. There  is information  attached  to the staff report  as to
  how the CAC  allocated  the funds  back in February.

  Ms. Averell  stated the item went before  the CAC  for their
  recommendations,  but HUD  had not released  the allocations  until  May.

  Mr. Salinas  asked Ms. Averell  to explain  the posting  notice.

  Ms. Averell  stated that once the allocations  are received,  the city prepares
  the documents  and then posts the consolidated  plan  and aru'iual action  plan
  on June 5'h because  there is 30-day  notice  for public  review  requirement.

  Council  MemberAvalos  has an issue as to how these funds  were allocated.
  There  is an item for $12,000  and asked the meaning  of "other  CDBG
  activities,"  and can that funding  be used for food  insecurity.

  Ms. Averell  stated the food programs  fall under  the public  service  grants.
  The public  service  grants have a cap of 15%  and during  the presentation  it
  was mentioned  the amount  was maximized.  The CAC  makes  these
  recommendations;  however,  the City  Council  can make  any changes  to the
  recornrnendations.

  Council  MemberAvalos  asked if the $12,000  can be allocated  into food
  insecurity  due to the need.

  Ms. Averell  stated not for the food insecurity  because  it falls under the
